sections.title: Asymptotes of a Hyperbola
sections.content: Straight lines that tangent the hyperbola at infinity. For x²/a² - y²/b² = 1, asymptotes are y = ±(b/a)x. The joint equation is x²/a² - y²/b² = 0. The hyperbola and its asymptotes differ only by a constant.

sections.title: Rectangular Hyperbola
sections.content: A hyperbola where a = b, and asymptotes are perpendicular. Standard equation: x² - y² = a² (Eccentricity e = √2). If rotated by 45°, it becomes xy = c², with parametric coordinates (ct, c/t).

sections.title: Conjugate Hyperbola
sections.content: The hyperbola x²/a² - y²/b² = -1 is conjugate to x²/a² - y²/b² = 1. They share the same asymptotes. If their eccentricities are e1 and e2, then (1/e1²) + (1/e2²) = 1.

sections.title: Co-normal Points
sections.content: Points on a conic where normals intersect at a common point. For an ellipse, a maximum of 4 normals can be drawn from a point. The eccentric angles of these 4 co-normal points sum to an odd multiple of π.

sections.title: Diameter of a Conic
sections.content: The locus of the midpoints of a system of parallel chords. For parabola y²=4ax (chord slope m), diameter is y = 2a/m. For ellipse, diameter is y = -(b²/a²m)x.

sections.title: Pair of Tangents
sections.content: The joint equation of a pair of tangents drawn from an external point (x1, y1) to any conic S=0 is given by SS1 = T². (Where S1 is the value of S at the point, and T is the tangent expression).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Confusing the parametric form of xy=c² (which is ct, c/t) with x²-y²=a² (which is a secθ, a tanθ).
2) Forgetting that (1/e1²) + (1/e2²) = 1 only applies to mutually conjugate hyperbolas.
3) Expanding SS1 = T² unnecessarily when the problem can be solved geometrically.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 targets advanced properties: Asymptotes, Rectangular Hyperbola properties, Co-normal conditions, and loci using SS1 = T² and diameters.

tricks.title: Conjugate Eccentricity Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If the eccentricity of a hyperbola is given, find the conjugate's eccentricity directly using 1/e1² + 1/e2² = 1.

tricks.title: Asymptotes Joint Equation Trick
tricks.explanation: The equation of Hyperbola (H), Asymptotes (A), and Conjugate Hyperbola (C) form an AP. H + C = 2A.
tricks.example: If H is x²/a² - y²/b² - 1 = 0, then A is x²/a² - y²/b² = 0, and C is x²/a² - y²/b² + 1 = 0.

tricks.title: Area of Triangle on Parabola
tricks.explanation: The area of a triangle formed by points t1, t2, t3 on y²=4ax is a² |(t1-t2)(t2-t3)(t3-t1)|. The area of the triangle formed by their tangents is EXACTLY half of this.
tricks.example: Saves solving a massive 3x3 determinant of coordinates.

tricks.title: Chord Subtending 90° at Vertex
tricks.explanation: If a chord of a parabola y²=4ax subtends a right angle at the vertex (0,0), it always passes through a fixed point on the axis: (4a, 0).
tricks.example: If asked for the fixed point of such a chord for y²=8x (a=2), it is instantly (8, 0).

tricks.title: Concyclic Points on Rectangular Hyperbola
tricks.explanation: If a circle intersects xy = c² at four points t1, t2, t3, t4, their product is always 1 (t1*t2*t3*t4 = 1).
tricks.example: If three points are t=2, t=3, t=1/2, the fourth intersection point must be t=1/3.

tricks.title: Maximum/Minimum Distance to Conic
tricks.explanation: The shortest or longest distance from a point to a conic ALWAYS lies along the normal drawn from that point to the conic.
tricks.example: To minimize distance from a line to a parabola, draw a tangent parallel to the line. The normal there gives the shortest distance.
